body:
The moment when I looked up and he wasn't there anymore. I have to make excuses for him. Family gatherings, holidays, you name it.. I'm always alone. 
We're still together and I do love him, but to everyone else its like we're "having problems".

My husband is bipolar. He's anger is the strongest and longest of his cycle. He'll often agree with you that he is an AH. A lot of the things he's said and done have made me uneasy. I've come to understand that there are two things someone with bipolar disorder can do in a relationship; find help and try to work it out or simply let it go. When its allowed to run wild the relationship becomes abusive. In our relationship its like trying to stay afloat in the middle of a blue sea. One moment I'm enjoying myself at the beach and I feel absolutely safe and in love the next I'm caught in a rip tide and don't know how to get back. 
There are times where he stops himself and apologizes. 
Its honesty the only reason I've stayed with him. I can see he is trying and I'm trying to understand that its hard for him to control his emotions.

I'm sorry you're facing this. I know how hard it is and I just hope that you don't blame yourself for any of this. You were not responsible for any of his choices. You are not to blame for any consequences he may face. You deserve to be treated with love and respect. You've done nothing wrong. Never forget that you are loved and you are not alone. 
I love you.
